note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a TRI 12; A06b TRI 12; L05 TRI 11(1), 11(2D), 17): ordinary naturalisation after 6 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Trinidad and Tobago, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Trinidad and Tobago for 12 months immediately prior to the application, and was either resident in Trinidad and Tobago, or in government service, or had partly such residence and partly such service for 5 out of 7 years prior to the 12-month period. ... n.a. ... Person acquires citizenship of another country otherwise than by marriage. Does not apply to citizens by birth or by descent. Loss cannot result in statelessness.
